title: Three Months Ago Shahid Kapoor Said No. Now He's Getting ₹18 Crore to Swap Souls with Janhvi Kapoor.
excerpt: After Cocktail 2 made him Bollywood's hottest bet again, Shahid locks a body-swap comedy called Adal Badal — with a fee that says the industry finally noticed
body:
Here's the thing about Bollywood: it has a very short memory. Three months ago, **Shahid Kapoor** walked away from director **Amit Ravindranath Sharma**'s soul-swapping comedy without even hearing the script. He'd just wrapped *Cocktail 2*, hadn't seen the numbers yet, and didn't fancy another romantic comedy on the back of one.

Fast-forward to this week. *Cocktail 2* has crossed **₹149 crore worldwide** and is still counting. Shahid is the most talked-about leading man in Hindi cinema. And that same script he refused? He just signed it — for ₹18 crore, plus a backend profit share if the film clicks.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZrnDU8ti80/


The film is called **Adal Badal**, and here's what we know: it's a high-concept body-swap comedy about a married couple on the verge of divorce who wake up one morning in each other's bodies. Think *Freaky Friday* meets Indian matrimony — the chaos of navigating your spouse's chai preferences, office politics, and in-laws while trapped in their skin. Sharma, who directed the wonderful *Badhaai Ho* (2018), is exactly the filmmaker to pull off something this tonally tricky: funny without being slapstick, emotional without being syrupy.

## The Pairing Nobody Saw Coming

Here's the real headline: Shahid's co-star is **Janhvi Kapoor**. It's their first film together, and on paper, the chemistry sounds electric. Janhvi's been quietly stacking credible work — *Mr. & Mrs. Mahi*, *Ulajh*, and the upcoming *Lag Ja Gale* with Tiger Shroff — but she hasn't had a big-ticket comedy pairing with a star of Shahid's current stature. This could be the one that redefines her as a mainstream leading lady.

The project is produced by **Sunir Kheterpal** with **Amazon MGM**, and shooting is locked to begin in **October 2026**. If the Cocktail 2 glow is any indication, Amazon is betting that Shahid in a comedy is a reliable theatrical-to-streaming pipeline.

## The ₹18 Crore Number

Let's talk about that fee, because it tells a story. After the quiet underperformance of *Jersey* (2022) and the modest showing of *Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya* (2024), Shahid was in a strange zone — respected, bankable in theory, but not commanding the top-tier fees of a Khan or a Ranbir. His reported salary for *Cocktail 2* was lower, a bet that the franchise's brand would carry the film.

It did. And now the market has corrected. ₹18 crore plus backend is a statement: Shahid Kapoor is no longer a value buy. He's premium again.

> "There was back-and-forth about taking on the project due to the budget, but everything has aligned now," a source told Bollywood Hungama.

That alignment, clearly, happened the week *Cocktail 2* crossed ₹100 crore.

## What Diaspora Audiences Should Know

With Amazon MGM producing, there's a near-certainty that *Adal Badal* will get a robust theatrical run followed by a Prime Video premiere — making it easily accessible for NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada without the usual scramble for limited screens. Shahid's rom-com energy plays exceptionally well with diaspora audiences: *Jab We Met* remains a cultural touchstone for Indian communities abroad, and *Cocktail 2*'s overseas numbers (nearly ₹57 crore and climbing) prove that hasn't changed.

The bigger picture: Shahid is now firmly in the space Bollywood needed him — reliable commercial star, versatile enough for both *Farzi* on streaming and mass entertainers in theatres. *Adal Badal* could cement that position if Amit Sharma brings even half the warmth he brought to *Badhaai Ho*.

## The Road Ahead

Shahid wraps **Farzi Season 2** for Raj & DK before pivoting to *Adal Badal*. Between a smash-hit sequel, a streaming franchise, and now a high-concept comedy with a fresh pairing, he's arguably having the best 2026 of any male Bollywood star not named Ranveer Singh.

And to think — all it took was saying no to the right film at the wrong time, and yes to it at exactly the right one.
